issues.description: Transcript text-cleaning pipeline complects normalization rules with data prep via opaque sed chain
issues.detail: The data.sh pipeline mixes file shaping, ID construction, and Chinese character normalization (full-width A, punctuation stripping) in one inline sed chain. The normalization rules are values (a small table of substitutions) intertwined with shell plumbing. Extract the rules into a named, reviewable mapping file or python script so the transformation is data, not code-shaped-as-pipeline.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh does not exit when unzip is missing, conflating warning with failure
issues.detail: The script echoes 'unzip is not installed' but continues, then later tries to invoke unzip and dies cryptically. The identity of 'precondition check' is complected with 'informational log'. Either exit non-zero on missing unzip, or do not check at all. The current shape is easy to write but not simple to reason about.

issues.description: Per-archive extraction blocks are three copy-pasted branches over a tiny data table
issues.detail: The three TAL_ASR-{1,2,3}.zip blocks are the same logic parameterized by (archive name, output subdir). That is data, not control flow. A loop over a small table of tuples is both simpler and shorter, and makes adding a fourth archive a one-line change instead of a copy-paste. Right now the structure hides the regularity.

issues.description: README links to a path that does not exist in the recipe
issues.detail: The README references ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml but the file lives at ./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml. A small incidental complexity introduced by an inconsistent path; the value (config location) and the identity (link) disagree. Fix the link.

issues.description: Expected utterance counts are magic numbers embedded in the heredoc
issues.detail: The counts 22467, 3208, 6072, 29386, 38924 are facts about the dataset, hard-coded inline. They are values that belong somewhere named (a manifest file or top-level constants block with a comment citing the dataset version), so a future maintainer can verify them against the publisher without grepping a heredoc.

issues.description: run.sh sets lm_train_text but use_lm defaults to false, complecting unused config with intent
issues.detail: use_lm=false yet --lm_config and --lm_train_text are still passed. The README results include an LM-decoded row. Either flip use_lm=true by default to match the documented results, or drop the LM args when the LM is disabled. As written, the script's intent is ambiguous.

review.summary: This is a recipe contribution that mostly follows the ESPnet template, so most of the code is symlinks and boilerplate. The substantive new code is local/data.sh and local/download_and_untar.sh, both of which suffer from the same shape of problem: small tables of facts (archive names, normalization rules, expected counts) are intertwined with control flow instead of being expressed as data. The result is easy to read line by line but not simple — adding a fourth archive or a new punctuation rule touches plumbing rather than a table. Nothing is broken in essence; the complexity is incidental, and a small amount of decomposition would make this recipe a clean template for future bootcamp contributions. The README path bug and the use_lm=false vs LM-decoded-results mismatch should be reconciled before merge.
